title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. For a number field K, T_K = Res_{K/Q} G_m and N_K : T_K -> G_m is the norm. V_K = Ker N_K is the norm-one torus. The preceding Proposition, whose conditions (i)-(iv) are partly on the previous page, characterises the quotient tori V' = V_K/R that are 'compact', i.e. R-anisotropic. Equivalently, the image of the units in V' is finite: (i) <=> (iii) V'(R) compact <=> (iv) V' is dominated by V_L. Here L = K ∩ K', K' is the largest subfield of the Galois closure on which complex conjugation τ is central, and the fields where τ is central are what Grothendieck calls 'weilien' (CM or totally real). So L is the largest CM-or-totally-real subfield of K, and L_0 = L ∩ R is its totally real part. The character-group argument on the previous page shows such an N lies in Z[I_K]^P = Z[I_L].

Corollary 2 (this page). Among the compact quotients V' of V_K there is a largest one, V_K^cpct, corresponding to a smallest R.
- Existence of a largest one: if V/R1 and V/R2 are compact, then V/(R1∩R2) embeds in their product and is compact.
- R is connected: V/R^0 is an isogenous cover of the compact torus V/R, hence also anisotropic.
- The norm N_{K/L} induces V_K^cpct ≅ V_L/V_{L_0} = V_L^cpct.
- Explicitly, R = Ker(N_{K/L}) · V_{L_0}, with V_{L_0} ⊂ V_K by inclusion of fields.

Proof of the last assertion.
- R contains Ker N_{K/L}, by (iv).
- R contains V_{L_0}: since N_{K/L}(λ) = λ^r for λ ∈ L (r = [K:L]), the image of V_{L_0} in V_L lies in V_{L_0}. That subtorus is the split-over-R part, whose real points modulo units are compact (unit rank of L equals unit rank of L_0).
- Hence R contains R' = Ker N_{K/L} · V_{L_0}.
- Since N_{K/L} : V_K -> V_L is surjective and λ ↦ λ^r is an epimorphism of V_{L_0}, we get V_K/R' ≅ V_L/N_{K/L}(V_{L_0}) = V_L/V_{L_0}. This is compact, so R = R'.
- In modern terms, R is the connected Zariski closure of the units of K inside V_K.

Definition. S_K^0 := T_K/R. N_K then induces ε, giving an exact sequence 1 -> V'_K -> S_K^0 -> G_m -> 1 and a map of exact sequences (*) from 1 -> V_K -> T_K -> G_m -> 1.

Functoriality.
- S_K^0 and (*) are contravariant in K via the norms N_{K'/K}, because 'largest compact quotient' is functorial in Q-tori.
- They are also covariant via the inclusions i_{K,K'}. These are not compatible with ε, but on the next page they are compatible with λ ↦ λ^r on G_m (diagram (**)).

The next page goes on to two results. First, the projective system of the S_K^0 is cofinally that of the weilien K, i.e. T_K/V_{K_0}. Second, there is a unique weight cocharacter i: G_m -> S_K^0 with ε∘i = λ^2.

This is precisely the connected Serre group S^K (Taniyama–Serre torus), whose limit over K is the connected Serre group S. It appears here as a candidate motivic Galois group for CM / abelian-type motives, with its weight homomorphism w.
errors: Notation slip on this page: in 'N_{L/K} induisant un isom.' and 'N_{L/K}(V_{L_0})' the map meant is N_{K/L}, as the logic of the argument requires.
'λ ↦ λ^n' should be λ ↦ λ^r, with r = [K:L]. This is harmless since any power map on a torus is an epimorphism.
Two steps are left implicit but are true: the surjectivity of N_{K/L} : V_K -> V_L, and the connectedness of Ker N_{K/L} (its character group Z[I]/Z is torsion-free). No real gap.

ideas.what: Largest anisotropic-over-R quotient of the norm-one torus V_K. It is identified with V_L/V_{L_0}, where L is the largest CM-or-totally-real subfield of K, via the norm. The kernel is the connected Zariski closure of the units.
ideas.modern_name: Connected Serre group S^K = T^K / closure of units; reduction of S^K to the maximal CM subfield
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968), building on Taniyama (1957) and Weil (1955, type A0 characters factor through the maximal CM subfield); later formulations by Langlands, Deligne, Milne

ideas.what: Term 'weilien' for fields on which complex conjugation is central (CM or totally real), plausibly honouring Weil's 1955 work on type A0 characters
Functoriality of S_K^0: contravariant via norms, covariant via inclusions compatible with λ ↦ λ^[K':K]; projective system over K
ideas.modern_name: Serre group as a projective limit S = lim S^K

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 -> V'_K -> S_K^0 -> G_m -> 1 compatible with T_K; on the next page, a weight cocharacter with ε∘i = λ^2

missed.claim: Historical priority. In 1965 Grothendieck independently constructs the connected Serre torus S_K^0, including its reduction to the maximal CM subfield and its weight structure, inside his 'Galois theory of motives'. This predates Serre's 1968 exposition. It suggests that the identification of the Serre group as the motivic Galois group of CM motives (usually attributed to Serre, Langlands and Deligne c. 1968–1982) was already on Grothendieck's agenda in 1965.
missed.quote: On désignera par S_K^0 le quotient T_K/R, donc on a une suite exacte 1 -> V'_K -> S_K^0 -> G_m -> 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a history-of-mathematics credit issue rather than new mathematics: the constructions themselves are now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct but standard today (the Serre group and the maximal CM subfield). The interest is historical: it is an early, independent and fairly complete construction of the Serre group by Grothendieck in a motivic context, unpublished, with the 'weilien' terminology.
transcription_corrections: 'que N_{L/K} induit un isom.' should read roughly 'puisque N_{K/L} induit un isom.'
'la fonction des plus grands quotients cpct' is likely 'le foncteur des plus grands quotients cpct' (of the torus T over Q).
